Outcome The contribution of the tourism industry to Uganda’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew from 2.7% in 2020 to 4.2% in part due to the diversification of Uganda’s tourism product offering. Building on the tourism product diversification successes of 2021, UNDP in partnership with Uganda Wildlife Authority and the private sector co-created the Rwenzori marathon – a sports tourism product curated to diversify Uganda’s tourism product range by harnessing the country’s rich topography; broaden meaningful community participation in the tourism value chain and drive domestic and international tourist traffic to experience the enchanted adventure that the Rwenzori offers.
To further stimulate the recovery of the tourism industry from the COVID-19 pandemic, UNDP also supported efforts to promote and market Uganda as a mountaineering tourism destination. In 2022, UNDP partnered with Uganda Tourism Board and Tooro Kingdom, to curate the Rwenzori Mountain Royal expedition documentary film detailing King Oyo Kabamba Nyimba Iguru IV of Tooro Kingdoms tourism experience summiting the Margharita Peak of Rwenzori Mountain. The documentary is being used to promote mountaineering tourism in the Rwenzoris whilst amplifying the conversation about the need to tackle biodiversity loss and the impact of climate change on the Rwenzori Mountain ranges.
Mining, industry and manufacturing contributed 1.8%, 27.1 % and 16.5% respectively to Uganda’s GDP in 2020/21 compared to 1.6%, 26.5% and 15.8% in 2019/20. The increased contribution of mining, industry and manufacturing can in part be attributed to the reforms in the policy and regulatory frameworks undertaken over the period 2021 – 2022 to create an enabling environment for investment in the sectors. Some of the policy and regulatory reforms supported by UNDP include the development of the National Industrialisation Policy, finalisation of the Mining and Minerals Bill 2021 which was passed into law by Parliament early this year and updating of the Uganda’s Mining Cadastral to inform evidence-based mineral licensing and investment decision making.
The unemployment rate was recorded at 11.9% (M: 10.4%; F: 14.1%) in 2021 while youth unemployment was estimated at 16.5% (M:13.5%; F:20.4%)
Ugandas competitiveness ranking improved from 117 (2020) to 115 out of 140 countries. This was due to a pickup in economic activity following the abolishment of lockdown measures, government policy interventions to support recovery of the private sector and recovery in regional and global demand.
Output 1 With the support of UNDP, two legal frameworks to support productivity, enhance competitiveness, and facilitate market access for MSMEs in the mining and tourism sectors were developed. UNDP supported the Government of Uganda to finalise the Mining and Minerals Bill 2021 which was passed into law by Parliament early this year. In addition, UNDP also supported the Government to prepare the Regulatory Impact Assessment of the Tourism Bill 2022 to inform decisions by Cabinet of Uganda on the proposed amendment to the Tourism Act 2008.
Output 2 With the support of UNDP, 43 inclusive green business models in agriculture and agribusiness, tourism, mining, manufacturing, renewable energy, construction, health and the creative arts industries have been scaled up resulting in thousands of jobs and livelihood opportunities for youth.
In addition, 140 innovative, locally appropriate sustainable development initiatives (micro enterprises) targeting underserved communities/groups and women have been developed and scaled up.
Furthermore, 140 MSMEs targeting vulnerable youth and women have been developed.
Output 3 As a result of UNDPs partnership with 43 youth-owned and focused enterprises in agriculture and agribusiness, tourism, mining, manufacturing, renewable energy, construction, health and the creative arts industries to pilot commercially viable innovative ideas and scale their enterprises, over 60,000 decent jobs and livelihood opportunities for youth have been created.
